title: Frictionless volunteer crawl fleet: one docker command -> remote public Postgres; study domestic-swarm vs GCP/AWS
description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

Stefan's deployment vision (2026-06-20), gated on #1161 (SQLAlchemy/Postgres provider) landing + verified for REMOTE use.

THE VISION: ~15-25 friends each run OpenWPM on their HOME machine by copy-pasting a SINGLE docker run command with NO local binds (no -v mounts). All crawl output streams to ONE publicly-reachable PostgreSQL instance. Zero local footprint / zero config for the volunteer.

HEADLINE RESEARCH QUESTION: quantify how much running from a swarm of domestic/residential IPs changes measured results vs running on GCP/AWS (datacenter IPs) — tracker presence, cloaking, bot-walls/CAPTCHA, block rates, ad/content served, cookie+fingerprinting behavior.

HARD REQUIREMENT + open architectural question: 'no local binds' means EVERY artifact must go to the remote DB, not just structured rows. OpenWPM unstructured data (response bodies, currently LevelDB on local disk) would still hit the local filesystem under #1161 alone (it is a STRUCTURED provider). To honor no-binds we must either (a) route unstructured content to the remote Postgres too (bytea / large objects), (b) route it to S3/GCS, or (c) disable unstructured capture. DECIDE this — it is the crux of the frictionless goal.

OPS/SECURITY for a public Postgres: per-volunteer credentials/schema isolation, network exposure hardening, abuse/quota limits, TLS, and schema-version coordination across heterogeneous volunteer runs.

ARTIFACT: study design in datadir/study-design-crawl-deployment.md (worker in progress). Depends-on: #1161 lands + confirmed to accept a remote DSN and run with all-remote storage.

comments.author: claude
comments.content:
Study additions (Stefan 2026-06-20):
- 4TH DEPLOYMENT VANTAGE: a single chunky server hosted on a UNIVERSITY network. Distinct from datacenter (GCP/AWS), single-domestic, and the volunteer residential swarm — university IPs have their own reputation/egress profile (often institutionally trusted, static, but not residential). So the vantage axis is now: datacenter (GCP/AWS) vs single-domestic vs residential-volunteer-swarm vs university-server.
- ANALYSIS METHODOLOGY: replicate the analysis from the stealth paper (Krumnow, Jonker, Karsch 2022, arXiv:2205.08890 — detectability / reliability / differential treatment of the measurement tool) ACROSS the vantages, to observe how much each vantage is detected/cloaked/served-differently. 'but maybe also more' = extend beyond their detection analysis to the broader tracking/differential measures. Note the leverage: the stealth instrument (#1154) removes the TOOL-detectability confound, so this study can isolate the VANTAGE-POINT effect cleanly — and a 2x2 of instrument(stealth/legacy) x vantage quantifies how much each axis contributes to measured differences.

comments.author: claude
comments.content: STORAGE DECISION (Stefan 2026-06-20): go DIRECT-to-public-Postgres (NOT edge-buffered split-sink). Trust model — volunteers are close friends, so the abuse/quota/credential-isolation hardening concern is WAIVED. Remaining technical (NOT solved by trust): (1) write-reliability of a direct DB connection over flaky home networks, (2) the unstructured-data-no-binds problem (response bodies must go to Postgres bytea / S3 / or be disabled). Relatedly, Stefan flagged a real forward-progress bug in the OLD parquet->S3 caching path (sites perpetually marked in-progress by the WQ but never committed/pushed) — investigating the StorageController's liveness guarantees separately.

comments.author: claude
comments.content: Study-design doc (datadir/study-design-crawl-deployment.md) updated: added 4th vantage (university server, H6), the Krumnow-2022 per-vantage tool-detectability replication + instrument×vantage 2×2 (§5.4), sharpened headline RQ to datacenter-vs-residential-swarm, and reframed §7.3 storage as an explicit Stefan decision — Option 1 direct-to-public-Postgres (this vision) vs Option 2 edge-buffered split-sink — incl. the no-binds unstructured-data sub-choice (bytea/S3/disable). comments.author: claude
comments.content:
Network-reliability assessment (Stefan + analysis, 2026-06-20): LOW risk of actually suffering. Volume trivial — 24GB/100k sites = ~240KB/site; ~1.2GB/volunteer over a multi-hour/day crawl = one ~240KB commit per ~10-30s per client. The only real failure mode is transient home-network disconnects, which degrade to RETRIES (not data loss) given (a) the StorageController commit-or-requeue forward-progress guarantee (worker in progress) + (b) a reconnect-with-backoff wrapper on the DB connection. No edge buffering needed -> reinforces the direct-to-Postgres decision.

PER-CLIENT SHARDING (Stefan): generalize the parquet provider's per-instance sharding (arrow_storage.py:42,59 — self._instance_id = random.getrandbits(32), stamped on every record for partitioning) to the SQLAlchemy provider: add an instance_id column to every table, set per provider instance. Buys per-client isolation (no cross-client lock contention) AND fixes the per-node-sequential visit_id/browser_id collision across volunteers in one move. QUEUED to run on #1161 after the current deps+DSN-wiring worker lands (avoid same-branch push race).

comments.author: claude
comments.content: Fleet-enabling: SQLAlchemy provider now stamps a per-instance instance_id (mirrors parquet) and makes it part of composite PKs on client-keyed tables, so many volunteers can write to one Postgres without visit_id/browser_id collisions. Pushed on PR #1161 (feat/sqlalchemy-postgresql-v2, b97e0b96), MERGEABLE.

comments.author: claude
comments.content: Research (datadir/research-self-hosted-object-storage.md) resolves the unstructured-data-no-binds sub-choice: route response bodies to a self-hosted S3-compatible store (option b). Recommendation: Garage (single 30MB binary, ~1GB RAM, AGPLv3) co-hosted with the public Postgres; SeaweedFS if scale grows. Integration is a near-drop-in CONFIG change (no provider code): OpenWPM's S3UnstructuredProvider forwards **kwargs to s3fs.S3FileSystem, which accepts endpoint_url. MinIO itself is dead upstream (repo archived Feb 2026) -- avoid. save_content resource-type whitelist + md5 dedup bound the footprint.

comments.author: claude
comments.content: Socket-reliability Phase 2 (relevant to the StorageController liveness/forward-progress investigation flagged 00:17): audited all 41 distinct wait/sleep/timeout/join sites in openwpm/ -> 28 KEEP (genuine hung-resource deadlines), 5 REPLACE wait-and-hope sites wireable to a real completion signal over the bidi socket chain, 4 MAYBE. Phase-3 fan-out = 5 workers (R1 Finalize-ack drain is the flagship; R2 deletes the #135 time.sleep(2) stopgap once R1 lands; R4 is the instrument-status signal-back). Full worklist in datadir/timeout-audit.md.

comments.author: claude
comments.content: Socket-reliability Phase 1 done: bidi finalize-ack work stacked on hardened sockets (#1180) as feat/bidi-on-hardening -> draft PR #1196. #1174's framing-safe ClientSocket.receive() is the canonical read path; #1129's data-socket back-channel (StorageController finalize_ack reply + DataSocket.finalize_visit_id_with_ack) landed as wired-but-uncalled infra for Phase 3 R1 to consume. #1129's TaskManager wiring was DROPPED + flagged needs-human: it assumed the abandoned refactor/event-driven-completion finalize path; on master finalize is FinalizeCommand->extension, not TaskManager. Phase 3 R1 must pick the call site.
